title: Unified Quake engine work packages
architecture: One shared TypeScript simulation and actor authority with per-source behavior, geometry, clocks, and execution profiles; private QC/QVM/native guest memory remains authoritative.

interpretation.edges: dependsOn governs review and acceptance order, not mandatory idle time before writing source. Running packages may use concrete published inputs while prerequisite packages run; stage labels only group related work.
interpretation.readiness: The lead dispatches only ports with concrete usable published inputs and exclusive write paths. Running tasks must not depend on failed or blocked packages. Published-input readiness is a lead judgment, not inferred from graph status; review and acceptance still require accepted dependencies.
interpretation.scope: All inherited and requested content/functionality remains required. Missing inputs, adapters, service access, or feasibility do not remove rows.
interpretation.evidence: Implementation is authorized. Latest committed checkpoint f87e5b86256e5b8ec0832f1ecc9e1b9691a4e5f6, tree b645d432b86776bff55192fdb1f8c7279226f7a5, adds Machine navigation, medic revival metadata and LMCTF administration/plasma, with the arena bot fixture corrected. Lead-reported scoped checks and compiled CPU/GL runs are recorded in docs/execution-status.md. Running states record implementation and joins, not full acceptance; graph validation proves no runtime or release result.
interpretation.proofBoundary: W05 starts from the reviewed source comparison and source census while W01 exhaustive inventory continues. W05/W41 establish usable ownership and source-time contracts; W74 supplies permanent behavior foundations for W42/W45/W49 and their expansions. W73 proves a real mixed-game executable in parallel with bulk imports. Native full execution remains required at W40.
interpretation.schedule: User-directed code-first sequence: import and join the engine, reach live human play, then optimize and finish broad hardening, regression, retail-reference, and release evidence. Existing strict type guards and a basic runner remain practical implementation tools. Illustrative dependency batches contain no time or completion estimate.
interpretation.earlyPlayable: W73 is the first actual mixed-game source executable; W66 integrates the full official/source-VM feature union. W40 adds native execution before final full-matrix and compiled release gates.

orchestrationPolicy.subdelegation: No unbudgeted subdelegation. The lead schedules every worker within the same active-agent budget.
orchestrationPolicy.announcement: Announce Model, Effort, and Task for each dispatch.
orchestrationPolicy.readyOrder: The lead prioritizes concrete-input-ready source imports with exclusive ownership, using ascending work-package ID where useful. Do not wait for prerequisite acceptance to begin source work against published interfaces; preserve acceptance dependency order.
orchestrationPolicy.writeOwnership: Only the current exclusive owner edits owned paths. Contract/build/application registrations have named owners. Read-only reviewers own no implementation paths.
orchestrationPolicy.correctionRouting: Return findings to the current path owner. Reopen only affected work and invalidate downstream evidence whose source/artifact fingerprints changed.

commits.policy: Commit verified bounded progress even without a remote.
commits.gitWriter: One lead-controlled Git index/commit writer, or isolated worktrees with reviewed integration.
commits.staging: Stage exact owned paths only. Concurrent workers never use blanket git add.
commits.message: Describe the concrete behavior/scope and relevant completed checks.
commits.completion: Verify the final combined snapshot and compiled binary before the final completion commit.

ownershipTransfers.condition: W08 accepted; W68 explicitly depends on W08 and owns later scheduler changes.
W18 accepted; W68 explicitly depends on W18 and owns later dispatch changes.
W66 accepted; W40 explicitly depends on W66 and adds real native guest registration.
W73 accepted; W66 explicitly depends on W73 and expands the same application entry.

tasks.title: Inventory required features, content, and common code lineage
deliverables: Pinned source and data identities
Feature ledger with an owner and acceptance case for every inherited or requested feature
Per-subsystem reuse, repair, consolidation, and replacement decisions
acceptance: Compare all three TS ports and original sources before selecting shared math, commands, cvars, filesystem, messages, entity lifetimes, resource ownership, rendering, media, and game interfaces.
Record each original/edition/expansion feature and deliberate behavior difference. Existing missing or broken implementations remain required work.

Enumerate Q1 id1, hipnotic, rogue, dopa, mg1, mg3 Dawn of the Machine, ctf, NetQuake, QuakeWorld, and the unresolved Quake 64 requirement; Q2 legacy base, xatrix, rogue, ctf, LMCTF, and rerelease base, Call of the Machine, The Reckoning, Ground Zero, Quake II 64; Q3 base and Team Arena with every inherited mode.
Distinguish Quake Live fixture provenance from official product scope. Never delete expected rows because supplied files or adapters are missing.

tasks.title: Capture authoritative behavior and performance baselines
deliverables: Reusable source-differential capture drivers and initial source-derived cases
Available actual Q2 native reference traces with source/data/runtime identities
Recorded reference environment and explicit deferred capture requirements
acceptance: Deliver the existing initial source-derived cases and actual Q2 native reference traces as implementation inputs, with repeatable commands and exact source/data/runtime identities. Broad retail, renderer, protocol, and performance capture continues at later verification and release gates; it is not a pre-import requirement.
Use independent original engines or source-derived oracles. Agreement among the three TS ports alone does not establish correctness.

Record available reference conditions and unresolved tolerances. W67–W71 must finish broad reference capture and adopt evidence-backed image/performance targets after imports, live human play, and optimization; W02 does not require those full campaigns of capture before code proceeds.
Keep retail content external and reference it by local path and hash. Capture commands and raw outputs for reruns.

tasks.title: Establish strict TypeScript policy and one Bun build entry
deliverables: Bun development, verification, and compiled Linux build commands
AST policy checks for every TS source, test, and tool
One owner for package, build, and CI aggregation
acceptance: Reject any, type assertions including as const, non-null assertions, unchecked escapes, and suppression directives across application code, tests, and tools.
Use strict TypeScript with checked external boundaries and exhaustive variants. Keep executable project tooling in TypeScript and avoid shell-script proliferation.

Qualify the real Bun Linux compile pipeline using implemented TypeScript tool entries and record compiler and runtime identities. W03 may be accepted before the production runtime entry exists; do not add a placeholder main or wait on W73. W73, W66, and W69 separately qualify the production engine from the same source graph used by Bun development.
Keep all package script, dependency, tsconfig, CI, and build registration edits with this owner. Other packages return concrete registration requests.

Keep current strict type guards and the practical build pipeline usable during code imports. Defer additional policy hardening and regression infrastructure until the integrated engine supports live human play and optimization; W67–W71 retain final strictness and regression qualification.

evidence: EARLY_TOOLING scope under the current W03 acceptance criteria; production engine acceptance remains W73/W66/W69.
Lead ran live typecheck, policy, and 32 combined tests on the foundation checkpoint.
Lead executed the actual compiled validator; the W03 owner verified compiled tool relocation.
review: Lead independently ran the compiled artifact and accepted the bounded early tooling scope.

tasks.title: Build verification interfaces and evidence accounting
deliverables: Typed case, fixture, execution, and evidence contracts
Basic runner with explicit outcomes and retained command output
Usable development execution profile
Current product manifest and expected-case interfaces for later full reconciliation
acceptance: Provide usable typed case and evidence interfaces plus a basic runner for actual imported code and live execution. Existing available manifests are inputs; exhaustive inventory and matrix generation do not block imports.
Report explicit PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED_MISSING_INPUT, TIMEOUT, and NOT_RUN outcomes with available source/artifact identities and retain failed command output.

Keep independent run outputs separate. Complete extended isolation, deterministic shards/resume, stale-evidence rejection, and exhaustive regression infrastructure at W67–W71 after imports, live human play, and optimization.

tasks.title: Freeze shared contracts and explicit game differences
deliverables: Shared math, identity, resource, world, session, rendering, movement, UI, and execution contracts
Versioned composition profile and capability contracts
Documented ownership and numeric/time boundaries
acceptance: Select proven shared code from the existing reviewed docs/reference-contracts.md comparison and verification/source-manifest.json census. W01 exhaustive feature reconciliation continues in parallel and does not block these contracts. Preserve stronger Q1/Q2 VM, media, campaign, ABI, and content contracts alongside Q3 instance ownership.
Separate map, movement, character, weapons, enemies, asset presentation, rules, and mod execution selections. Preserve original defaults and make each requested override explicit.
Define family differences as typed profiles, not appended enum slots, generic untyped records, or parallel whole-engine trees.
Own all shared interfaces and headers. Publish concrete worker signatures so dependents can start while the remaining contracts finish, without runtime stubs or casts.

Freeze combat-before-mutation, campaign-versus-round authority, source-time ordering/ties, typed callback returns, guest byte views, headless simulation, and per-seat presentation contracts before accepting dependent providers; source imports may use the concrete published interfaces while these proofs finish.

tasks.title: Reuse and qualify Linux SDL2 and native library bindings

SDL2 windows, OpenGL context, events, audio devices, and controllers
Approved Vorbis and FreeType entry points and resource lifetimes
acceptance: Compare existing bindings and retain proven implementations. Only this platform owner imports bun:ffi.
Run real pushed SDL events, context/procedure lookup, queued audio, controller routing, partial-startup cleanup, and repeated open/close checks.
Keep FFI descriptor tuples typed and native buffers alive through their actual use. Store GLSL as embedded TypeScript strings through the rendering contract.
Support graphical and display-free dedicated startup. Game DLL/SO logic is never executed through native dlopen, a host emulator, or WASM.

tasks.title: Close missing required content and Quake 64 manifests

Reconcile every expected official campaign, expansion, executable, and localization/media fixture against available files.

tasks.title: Consolidate common engine services and session lifetimes

Explicit server/client/world/connection/module lifetimes
Initial frame scheduler with an isolated replaceable dispatch contract
acceptance: Consolidate common lineage only where W01 and source-profile tests establish equivalence. Retain deliberate family parsing, arithmetic, and timing differences.
Run repeated game, map, renderer, and module switches with distinct session owners; Q1/Q2 process globals must not leak between sessions.
Keep server simulation, client prediction, render resources, random generators, clocks, and published snapshots independently owned.
Preserve common console/config behavior, command ordering, resource lookup, recovery, and idempotent shutdown without carrying duplicated engine loops.
Order equal source deadlines explicitly and replay Q264/LMCTF command, ammo, weapon-event, and effect behavior without replacing source clocks with one arbitrary tick.

Resolve geometry, game implementation, behavior profile, and presentation mounts independently. Detect conflicts before launch.
Carry inherited pure/download and mod lookup requirements through typed filesystem services.
Reject an unknown requested mod or unresolved composition with a precise missing requirement. Never select base game silently.

Verify scalar pose and geometry output against original format/renderer references before backend rendering.

Q1/Q2 lighting profiles and Q3 material/shader compiler

Prove foreign actor hulls on real Q1 maps without BRUSHLIST while preserving stock hull results, contents, startsolid/allsolid, moving submodels, and measured trace cost.

Preserve resource lifetime, source draw ordering, retained state, cinematics, stencil operations, portals, sky, fog, lightstyles, and per-family effects.
Prepare complete scenes once for both actual backends, including split-screen views, independent HUDs, UI previews, and overlays.
Keep commands typed and instance-owned. Do not add a parallel renderer per game family.
Preserve required runtime camera/spline behavior and independent per-seat view calculation.

Retain original save semantics where representable and use the complete unified format for mixed sessions. Preserve unknown version rejection and content identity checks.
Verify uninterrupted play against save, process exit, fresh load, and continuation, including death/retry, autosave, intermission, and repeated map transitions.

Replay predicted movement, weapon events, animation, and ammo against authoritative source-order execution, including independent movement/arsenal choices.

Quake II 64 physics and game/cgame agreement

Correct the Q264 n64_physics client/server discrepancy and verify prediction against the exact authoritative selected movement.
Keep weapon, animation, and collision bounds ownership explicit so character and arsenal overrides do not substitute the wrong movement.
Exercise source game/cgame exported prediction as well as direct TS movement against real maps and command traces.
Replay predicted movement, weapon events, animation, and ammo against authoritative source-order execution, including independent movement/arsenal choices.

Match source jump/air/ground/water/step/knockback traces and all base/Team Arena movement variants.
Run Q3 movement with independently selected Q1/Q2 characters and arsenals through the same source-order contract.
Reject product-specific enum/stat collisions by construction instead of making Q3 numeric values universal.
Replay predicted movement, weapon events, animation, and ammo against authoritative source-order execution, including independent movement/arsenal choices.

An explicit decision not to build an unneeded compiler does not waive QuakeC execution, missing-source extraction, or any requested composition.

Executable-image, CPU, import, ABI, TLS, and exception contracts
Traceable guest instruction/host-call evidence

Define exact register/flag/stack/FPU state and instruction/import failure records before parallel loader and CPU implementation.
Keep guest memory private to its execution owner while exposing reviewed semantic bindings to the shared actor store.
All guest instructions execute in TypeScript. Native execution, WASM, external emulators, and replacement TS game logic cannot satisfy this lane.

Compare loaded bytes and export addresses with independent executable-format references.

Resolve required libstdc++, libm, libgcc_s, and libc interfaces through TypeScript guest runtime services.
